thread:
mel: FYI support flagged 4 customers earlier reporting repeated 401s + duplicate billing after updating to the latest TS SDK release. raising an incident.
samir: ACK. any repro / affected SDK version info?
mel: tickets: https://redwood.support/t/6481, https://redwood.support/t/6482, https://redwood.support/t/6483
infra-eng: looking at edge logs — clients send auth header, upstream returns 401, then immediate client retry. we see pairs of near-identical POSTs per request id
infra-eng: example log:
```
[2026-03-04T09:07:12Z] req=ff12 POST /v1/generate 401 "x-api-client=***" upstream=auth-mismatch
[2026-03-04T09:07:12Z] req=ff12 POST /v1/generate 401 "x-api-client=***" upstream=auth-mismatch retry=1
```
samir: that pattern matches the regen we merged yesterday for SDK templates. the new templates changed header key -> `x-api-client` and also changed header ordering logic in the emitted HTTP request
devex-oncall: CI note: the cross-regenerate job pulled the latest openapi-generator image (un-pinned) on master; our CI for client gen uses a pinned generator, so generated templates diverged between what merged and what CI validated
jia: so header order + key change could break our router auth/dedupe? how does that double-bill customers?
samir: router dedupe key is currently derived from canonical request string which includes header serialization order. if header order changes, dedupe misses and both original + retry get through and are billable
qa-ally: root cause diff summary: unpinned generator -> regenerated SDKs (TS + Py) altered header serialization -> edge auth/dedupe heuristics failed -> clients saw 401s and retried -> duplicate requests recorded
mel: immediate mitigations?
infra-eng: short-term: make auth/header matching tolerant — normalize header names/values for auth check and dedupe. can canary in ~2h
devex-oncall: opening an emergency PR to the router to canonicalize headers (sort by lowercased header name) before fingerprinting: https://github.com/redwood/router/pull/1223
samir: on SDK side we'll patch templates to restore previous `x-api-key` header name and stable header emission. cutting patch releases for TS and Python (will be 0.43.1)
samir: patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/sdk-templates/pull/820 — adds explicit header key and preserves insertion order
qa-ally: also adding a cross-SDK test fixture: generate a canonical fingerprint from Python/TS/Go generated clients and compare to golden to detect regressions in future
devex-oncall: CI guard PR opened to fail regen merges if generator image != pinned in repo: https://github.com/redwood/ci-config/pull/210
jia: customer comms plan: inform affected customers we identified the issue, rolled a canary for tolerant auth/dedupe, releasing SDK patches, and issuing credits for duplicate charges. drafting messages now and will update tickets when canary is green
mel: runbook additions: if auth/401 spikes + retry concurrency > X, check recent regen commits, generator version mismatch, and recent sdk-template merges
samir: repro steps for engineering team:
1. switch openapi-generator to latest (unpin)
2. regen TS + Python templates
3. run a simple request and capture raw headers via tcpdump / proxy
```
# quick repro (TS)
import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk'
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: 'REDACTED' })
await c.chat.create({ model: 'x', input: 'hi' })
// inspect proxy logs for header ordering and key
```
infra-eng: note: to simulate dedupe miss, reorder headers client-side before send
mel: timeline: router canary in ~2h, SDK patch published <90m, CI guard merged after canary. support to notify customers once canary is healthy
qa-ally: adding post-incident tasks: add regen checksum verification in merge workflow and unit-tests comparing canonicalized request fingerprints between generated clients
mel: thanks all. follow up in this thread with canary results and PR links. :thumbsup:
(reacted with :rotating_light: by support-bot)
